title: DX Cohort Signal Hub: Coordinated SDKs, Docs & Quickstarts Initiative
creator: Lina Martín
description: Establish a lightweight 'Signal Hub' to track cohorts of developer adopters across SDKs, docs, and quickstarts. The hub will centralize signals (activation, time-to-first-call, error rates, churn) for initiative-level OKRs and enable PMs/Design/Eng to run weekly cohort reviews. Focus is on incrementally shipping a minimum viable signal model that integrates SDK telemetry, docs analytics, and quickstart completion events.
updates: 2025-11-07 - Created ticket; initial scoping workshop with ENG, DX Research, and Docs (Lina, Daniel, Priya). Agreed on MVP signals: time-to-first-call, success rate on quickstart, SDK install failures, API latency by route. Action: ENG to validate telemetry event names.

2025-11-10 - ENG sync: Daniel and Sam reviewed existing telemetry schema. Trade-off discussed: enrich events with user properties vs. keep lightweight IDs to avoid PII. Decision: start with hashed cohort_id + event_type to avoid immediate GDPR scope and iterate if we need richer signals. Action: ENG to add cohort_id to sdk.init and quickstart.complete events (RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/4589).

2025-11-12 - PM/Design review: Lina reviewed proposed dashboard wireframes in Confluence (https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DX/pages/Signal+Hub+Wireframes). Design feedback: emphasize retention curves and a single view to compare SDK vs docs cohorts. Follow-up: Design to deliver hi-fi mockups by 2025-11-18.

2025-11-15 - Data infrastructure spike complete (ENG): validated event ingestion path to analytics cluster. Proof-of-concept SQL queries and a lightweight materialized view are in the analytics repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/analytics/tree/feature/dx-signal). Note: current view aggregates daily and is eventually consistent; may miss sub-minute signals—acceptable for MVP.
2025-11-18 - Design delivered hi-fi mockups; PM and Eng held design review. Minor UX change: add cohort comparison toggle and CSV export. Decision: defer export to post-MVP (due to scope).

2025-11-20 - Internal demo of MVP dashboard (alpha) to Growth and Solutions teams. Feedback: include a breakdown by onboarding pathway (docs vs SDK quickstart). Action: add onboarding_path tag to quickstart.complete events (ENG ticket created).
2025-11-21 - Updated acceptance criteria and flagged a dependency on ENG-2907 (analytics retention config). Scheduling a canary roll for a small subset of new signups next week.
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: sdk.init, quickstart.start, quickstart.complete events emit cohort_id and onboarding_path for >=90% of new users in canary segment.
Analytics: materialized daily cohort table with time-to-first-call, quickstart completion rate, and SDK install failure rate.
Dashboard: single-page Signal Hub with cohort selection, retention curve, and top failure reasons; accessible to PM/Design/Eng teams behind SSO.
Reporting: weekly automatic digest emailed to initiative stakeholders and a Slack alert for regression in quickstart completion (>20% drop week-over-week).
risks: Analytics retention limits could surface incomplete cohorts if retention window shorter than expected (dependency ENG-2907).
Over-instrumentation risk: adding user PII fields would increase compliance scope—mitigated by using hashed cohort_id for MVP.
Performance: materialized view currently daily; if product needs sub-daily signals, additional infra will be required and increase cost.
next_steps: ENG: land telemetry PR and run canary for 5% of new signups (owner: Sam, due 2025-11-28).
Data: finalize materialized cohort table and onboard dashboard queries (owner: Priya, due 2025-11-30).
Design: iterate on comparison UX and provide final assets for implementation (owner: Mei, due 2025-11-25).
PM: validate weekly digest recipients and KPI thresholds; prepare stakeholder demo for 2025-12-02 (owner: Lina).
